# Draft Output: PM-10 Plan Scope Management
**AI-generated by:** Alson (A.I Agent)

## Decision Requested

Approve a formal but lightweight scope-management approach for Lead Lab's proposed self-hosted web application. The approach controls the transition from the WordPress baseline without treating the proposed web-app delivery plan as an approved scope baseline.

## Proposed Scope Approach

### Scope Development

1. Use PM-11 to confirm participant, administrator, IT, media, and approver needs.
2. Separate replacement requirements from proposed product enhancements.
3. Use PM-12 to define the committed MVP boundary, deliverables, exclusions, assumptions, constraints, and success measures.
4. Use PM-13 to decompose the approved scope into a backlog or work structure.
5. Link each approved requirement to a feature, work item, and acceptance test.
6. Do not treat the existing WordPress backlog or the proposed web-app plan as the approved custom-app baseline.

### Provisional Working Scope

The following is a proposed input for PM-11 and PM-12, not an approved commitment:

- One private Lead Lab community.
- Invite-only member access.
- Participant, moderator, and administrator roles.
- Community posts, comments, categories, and announcements.
- Recorded sessions with embedded videos and downloadable materials.
- Search and category/date filters.
- Events and meeting links.
- Responsive desktop, tablet, and mobile use.
- Protected application routes and file downloads.
- No payments, public discovery, direct messaging, native apps, or multi-community support.

### Scope Authority

| Decision | Proposed authority | Current evidence status |
|---|---|---|
| Scope-management approach | PM | PM direction not yet recorded for this approach |
| Requirements approval | PM with requester, IT, media, and participant input | Named approver not recorded |
| MVP scope baseline | PM or authorized sponsor | Not yet confirmed |
| Launch acceptance | LeadLab Director | Recorded in the request brief and dependencies register |
| Technical implementation | Technical lead and IT team | Technical lead name and server capability not recorded |
| Scope maintenance | Named scope owner, currently TBD | No owner confirmed in artifact index |

### Acceptance Approach

Acceptance will be evidence-based. Every approved scope item will have a testable outcome and a named acceptance authority.

The proposed delivery gates are:

| Gate | Proposed evidence |
|---|---|
| Environment ready | Runtime, database, staging, HTTPS, backup location, and operators confirmed |
| Vertical slice | Account creation, login, access restriction, lesson publishing, video playback, protected download, revocation, and staging deployment work |
| Feature complete | All approved MVP requirements pass on staging; no new launch features added |
| Launch decision | Security, participant testing, content, restore, support procedures, and final approval complete |

These gates remain proposed until the PM approves the scope-management approach and confirms the schedule process separately.

### Change Control

All proposed scope changes will follow this route:

1. Record the change in the change log as `Proposed`.
2. Identify the affected requirement, feature, deliverable, exclusion, or acceptance condition.
3. Assess schedule, cost, risk, quality, security, resource, and fallback effects.
4. Obtain explicit PM direction before changing the scope baseline or backlog.
5. Obtain LeadLab Director approval for changes that affect launch commitment, participant experience, or final acceptance.
6. Update the approved scope record, backlog, traceability, and tests only after approval.
7. Keep rejected, deferred, and unresolved changes visible.

The proposed plan's September 2 feature cut-off is a recommended control, not an approved baseline date.

### Scope Review Cadence

- Review scope at the end of PM-11, PM-12, and PM-13.
- Review scope at each proposed delivery gate.
- Review immediately when the platform direction, access model, participant data, video approach, or launch content changes.
- Run PM-14 after the scope baseline exists and delivery begins.
- Run PM-15 after staging acceptance evidence and participant review exist.

## Required Inputs Before Baseline

- Explicit direction on whether the custom web-app proposal replaces the WordPress baseline.
- Named scope owner and PM decision authority.
- Confirmed server runtime and database.
- Participant volume and participant-data handling rules.
- Required September program content inventory.
- Video-hosting and URL-sharing acceptance decision.
- Approved launch requirements and exclusions.

## Quality Result

The draft addresses PM-10's purpose and defines scope development, acceptance, traceability, change control, authority, and review triggers. It does not establish a scope baseline or approve the web-app product direction.
